Native storage reply timing: QOS dc0c65c plus trace, FP-RISC e138e654332f, QEMU 11.1.3 RV64 virt, Darwin arm64.
Build command: FPRISC_ROOT=<pinned-checkout> python3 tools/store-wait-bench.py --reply-trace <new-directory>
Each run boots from a new disk, appends 128 eight-byte events, and checks every growing replay.
Trace hook reads the 10 MHz guest mtime after copying the reply and immediately before mailbox release publication.
The second read follows successful selective receive. Sender, caller, and correlated ID are checked.
One client with one request in flight. All per-operation percentiles use nearest rank, pooling three boots.
Zero-gap is a hypothetical ceiling: subtract each individual observation gap from its own call duration, then take percentiles.
This includes ordinary scheduling and dequeue overhead. Blocking receive would still have those costs.
Fresh controls disable timestamps and counters. All six traced and six control boots must validate.
Raw rows below are in 100 ns ticks. Absolute clocks restart on each boot.
